terra.problem: The passage does not say that nobody was loading wagons.
“I bake for a living” presents Papa as a baker, which he never calls himself.
The passage does not say Daniel would never forget what he saw.
The Jordan's location and Daniel being far from home are facts outside the passage and have no references.
The Nile's connection to Egypt is a fact from outside the passage with no reference. The passage also does not state that the scene is not in Egypt.
The lighting-package joke makes the man's appearance the joke.
The “Just some guy” joke makes the man's appearance the joke.
The text says the men did not see the vision, not that they did not know what they were running from.
The text does not say the men lacked nerve. Their not seeing the vision also does not establish that there was no man for them to call to.
Saying the men did not have nerve puts them down.
The text tells Daniel to stand, but does not say he needed to be on his feet to hear the words.
The first-person quotation is introduced as “the reason given,” without identifying who is speaking.
The first-person quotation is introduced as “the reason,” without identifying who is speaking.
“Babylon is where Daniel's story began” adds a fact outside the passage without a reference, and Daniel's story begins with Jerusalem being besieged.
“The text says” does not identify the speaker of the first-person quotation.
The explanation repeats that Michael is one of the chief princes without adding anything, making it noticeably flat.
“The text says” does not identify who is speaking in the first-person quotation.
Identifying Elijah as a prophet from Israel is a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
“The text says” does not identify who is speaking in the first-person quotation.
The explanation is generic and mechanical, with no distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The text says Daniel set his face toward the ground. It does not say he was face down or establish that he stayed in one place.
The first-person quotation is introduced as what “the text says,” rather than identifying Daniel as its speaker.
The first-person quotation is introduced as what “the text says,” rather than identifying Daniel as its speaker.
“A moment ago” adds a time interval the text does not give.
“After a night like that” adds a time of day the passage does not give.
The speaker says the prince of Greece will come when he has gone forth, not that he will come after the fight.
“Those men are long gone” adds an elapsed time and assumes where the men are.
The explanation is generic and mechanical, with no distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
